description: A bear the swamp claimed and gave back. Mushrooms fruit on its shoulders; its jaw closes like a bog-gate.
lore: It did not go into the swamp. The swamp arrived. This was a wood bear on wood-bear ground, doing the ordinary work of being one, and then the land re-remembered itself around it across a few slow years — and now the trail it knows is four feet under, and the trees it knows are stumps standing in water, and it is still walking the round. Out at the same bank. Up a slope that is not there any more. Three long pauses at nothing in particular. Back.

You can read how long from its shoulders, because moss does not take on an animal that moves, and the red-caps come in after the moss, in tiers, and only where a thing has stood still through a great deal of wet. [[characters/a6d7323d|Gunnar]] dates them the way other people date weather. He keeps his measurements to himself as a rule and gives this one away free, because the animal is not lost and is not looking for anything, and that makes it worse to meet: it is not wandering across your path, you are standing in the middle of its wood. The jaw comes down like a gate dropping, with no warning in it at all, and from where the bear is you were never anywhere but underfoot.
gm_notes: Law IV played straight for once: the Drift as a thing that happens TO a creature. The mushroom tiers are a field-usable clock for how long a Mireback has been standing — reusable by any agent wanting to age one. Gunnar's one shared measurement is deliberate: it costs him something, which is why it lands.
